title: Hearing Goldkette at the Steel Pier and Roseland
summary: Waters places the Goldkette band at Roseland during his time with Fletcher, then heard it in person at Atlantic City's Steel Pier while playing nights with Charlie Johnson at the Paradise Inn.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it

blocks.x: When you were saying you were knocked out by the Goldkette Band, are you speaking of the band that had Beiderbecke or -
The band that came to New York -
at the Roseland Ballroom, that's the band I'm talkin' about. 'Cause I was working at the Roseland Ballroom with Fletcher Henderson -
No, not the same time, the same period.
We would all go on the road and come back and they would have another band that stay there a couple of weeks, during when we'd come back, see. 'Cause Fletcher was there before Goldkette, you know.
Yeah, sure. Did you hear Goldkette's band at Roseland, or were you not able to attend?

No, I heard Rose-, I heard [ ], I heard Goldkette's in person at Steel Pier in Atlantic City, because I was working in Atlantic City with Charlie Johnson's band and we only worked at night, at a place called the Paradise where he got his name, of Paradise Inn. We worked at the Paradise Inn in Atlantic City and the Paradise here in New York. That's where the name Charlie Johnson and his Paradise Ten, that's where the name was acquired. So I, so we didn't work that afternoon, and the Steel Pier and other pier opened up at 3 o'clock every afternoon. And you could go up there on the Boardwalk and listen to those, stand right in front of Bix and those cats, you know what I mean? And that's why I know, I mean, sayin' it was a fantastic band.
